title: Is DeepSeek V4.1 Flash good enough to be the default coder?
hypothesis: On our own replayed tasks, Flash accepts at least 85% as many tasks as GLM 5.3 at no more than 25% of the cost per accepted task.
human_gate: Frank signs the routing.schema.json change that reorders the code class.

runs_on.why: T1 run (12 tasks x 3 arms, repeated). The laptop never runs T1 or higher, so this waits for the Railway worker.

success_rule: Directional only (design.decision_effect none): accepted_rate(flash) >= 0.85 * accepted_rate(glm) AND cost_per_accepted(flash) <= 0.25 * cost_per_accepted(glm). If both hold, the result justifies a confirmation run at 10 or more attempts per cell; only that confirmation can make Flash the code-class primary and GLM the escalation.
kill: Directional pilot at one run per cell, below the 10-per-cell floor, so no result changes routing. Stop after 12 tasks x 3 arms or $6, whichever comes first. If Flash accepts under 70% of what GLM accepts, GLM stays primary and no confirmation run is scheduled.

next_gate.receipt: lab/results/EXP-001.md with the per-arm table from receipts

decision_it_feeds: Order of the code-class chain in fleet/routing.schema.json.

prior_evidence.claim: Vendor-independent leaderboard: DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 scored 88.8% on SWE-bench Verified at about $0.01 per test, Kimi K3 93.4% at $0.76, DeepSeek V4 Pro 77.4%, GLM 5 71.4%.
prior_evidence.caveat: SWE-bench Verified is public and likely contaminated. The listing says V4 Flash 0731, our route is v4.1-flash, and the quoted price ($0.44/$1.32) differs from Token Pass ($0.15/$0.60). Treat as a reason to test, not as proof.

prior_evidence.claim: A user report prefers GLM over Flash on design and coding issues Flash struggled with.
prior_evidence.source: reddit.com/r/opencode, GLM 5.3 Flash vs DeepSeek V4.1 Flash thread
prior_evidence.caveat: One anecdote. It is the reason GLM stays the incumbent arm.

design.note: 12 tasks x 3 arms is one attempt per cell, below the 10-per-cell floor (lab/packs.json sample_floor_per_cell). Directional pilot: it changes no routing.
